explanation: Merge the two inorder value sequences, retaining duplicates, then build a balanced tree using the required upper-middle index of each half-open range. Empty inputs are handled without special node assumptions.
timeComplexity: O(m+n): inorder traversal, two-pointer merging and midpoint reconstruction each visit the total input size linearly.
spaceComplexity: O(m+n) values and newly allocated output nodes; traversal stacks use input heights and balanced rebuilding adds O(log(m+n+1)) frames.
attribution: Original Python implementation authored for EPI Practice from its displayed contract and independently authored C# solution; no upstream reference source adapted.
correctness: Inorder traversals produce the two sorted multisets. Standard merging preserves every occurrence. Recursive reconstruction chooses exactly the prescribed midpoint of each half-open range, so both the sorted contents and the required canonical structure follow.
walkthrough: The BSTs [4,1,7] and [6,2,9] merge to [1,2,4,6,7,9]. Midpoint construction gives root 6, left subtree rooted at 2 and right subtree rooted at 9. Level order is [6,2,9,1,4,7].
edgeCases: Either input tree may be empty.
Duplicate values from either input are retained.
The midpoint convention matters because this corpus compares structure.
